questions.statement: Which sentence uses the present continuous correctly?
questions.context: Present continuous, San Juan, grado 11, W02.

options.text: She is studying for the biology test right now.
options.feedback: Correct! The present continuous is the auxiliary 'is' plus the participle 'studying', and 'right now' marks the action as happening at this moment.

options.text: She study for the biology test right now.
options.feedback: Incorrect! The bare verb 'study' is the simple present, which describes a repeated habit instead of an action in progress.

options.text: She is study for the biology test right now.
options.feedback: Incorrect! After the auxiliary 'is' the verb must be the participle 'studying', never the base form 'study'.

options.text: She studying for the biology test right now.
options.feedback: Incorrect! The participle 'studying' can never stand on its own here, because it requires the auxiliary 'is' in front of it.

questions.explanation:
El presente continuo se forma con el verbo 'to be' en presente mas el gerundio. Sirve para acciones que estan ocurriendo ahora mismo o que estan de forma temporal. Reconocer los marcadores 'now', 'currently' o 'at the moment' es la via rapida para identificar el tiempo verbal.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'They ____ (wait) for the bus in Caguas.'
questions.context: Present continuous with the verb to be, Ponce, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect! The auxiliary 'is' is singular, and the subject of this sentence is the plural 'they'.
Incorrect! 'Waits' carries the -s of the singular third person, and a simple present cannot describe an action still in progress.
Correct! 'They' is plural, so the auxiliary of the present continuous is 'are' in front of the participle 'waiting'.
Incorrect! 'Wait' is the bare form, and the progressive would need 'are waiting' with a plural subject.

questions.explanation:
En el presente continuo el auxiliar y el gerundio deben concordar con el sujeto. Es el error mas comun de la unidad: escribir 'is waiting' con 'they' o 'are waiting' con 'he'. Revisar siempre el sujeto antes de conjugar.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct negative form: 'He ____ (not / read) the newspaper at the moment.'
questions.context: Present continuous negatives, Carolina, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect! 'Don't' is the auxiliary of I, you, we and they, and it never carries the third person ending.
Correct! The negative present continuous is 'is not' plus the participle, which contracts to 'isn't reading'.
Incorrect! After 'isn't' the verb must be the participle 'reading', and the base form 'read' is impossible there.
Incorrect! The negative needs the auxiliary 'does not', so the -s in 'not reads' sits in the wrong place.

questions.explanation:
El negativo del presente continuo sigue el mismo esquema que el afirmativo: auxiliar 'to be' mas 'not' mas gerundio. La forma contracta mas frecuente es "isn't, aren't" y "am not" aunque tambien se admite la forma completa.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which question is correct?
questions.context: Present continuous questions, Bayamon, grado 11, W02.

options.text: Do you use the library room now?
options.feedback: Incorrect! 'Do you use' is a question in the simple present, while the marker 'now' asks for the present continuous.

options.text: Are you use the library room now?
options.feedback: Incorrect! After the auxiliary 'Are' the verb must be the participle 'using', and the base form 'use' is impossible.

options.text: You are using the library room now?
options.feedback: Incorrect! 'You are using ...?' keeps the order of a statement, and a question puts the auxiliary in front of the subject.

options.text: Are you using the library room now?
options.feedback: Correct! 'Are you using' has the auxiliary before the subject and the participle 'using' after it, which is question form in the continuous.

questions.explanation:
Para preguntar por lo que esta pasando se invierte el orden del presente continuo: el auxiliar 'to be' abre la frase, luego va el sujeto y despues el gerundio. El gerundio nunca lleva auxiliar al final.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which is the correct gerund form of the verb 'to run'?
questions.context: Present continuous spelling, Arecibo, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect! 'Runing' drops the doubled consonant that the spelling requires when the stem ends in one consonant after a short vowel.
Incorrect! 'Runnning' triples the n, and English never writes three of the same consonant in a stem like this.
Incorrect! 'Runeing' is not a spelling of any English form; the participle keeps the spelling of the base verb.
Correct! 'To run' doubles the n before -ing, so the participle is written 'running'.

questions.explanation:
Hay tres reglas para formar el gerundio. Si el verbo termina en -e se quita la -e, si termina en vocal breve tensa se duplica la consonante final, y en los demas casos se añade -ing directamente. 'To be' da 'being' y es la excepcion a la primera regla.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which is the correct gerund form of the verb 'to swim'?
questions.context: Present continuous spelling, Humacao, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect! 'Swiming' drops the doubled m, and the spelling of the participle never changes the base form.
Correct! 'To swim' doubles the final m before -ing, and that is exactly how the participle 'swimming' is written.
Incorrect! 'Swimm ing' splits one word in two, and a participle is always written as a single word.
Incorrect! 'Swuming' changes the vowel of the base verb, which no English spelling rule allows.

questions.explanation:
La duplicacion de la consonante ocurre tras vocal breve tensa, como en 'swim', 'run', 'sit' o 'begin'. El objetivo es que la palabra conserve dos sílabas en el gerundio. Si el sonido ya es largo, no se duplica, como en 'open' o 'travel'.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'My sister ____ (make) a cake for the party right now.'
questions.context: Present continuous with third person, Aguadilla, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Correct! 'My sister' is a singular subject, so the auxiliary of the present continuous is 'is' before 'making'.
Incorrect! 'Are' is the plural auxiliary, and it disagrees with the singular subject 'my sister'.
Incorrect! After 'is' the verb must be the participle 'making', and the base form is impossible in that slot.
Incorrect! 'Makes' is the simple present of a singular subject, which describes a habit rather than an action in progress.

questions.explanation:
El presente continuo tiene el mismo auxiliar que el presente simple: 'am', 'is' o 'are' segun el sujeto. Lo que cambia es el verbo principal, que siempre pasa a gerundio. Revisar la concordancia del auxiliar es la mitad del trabajo.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'I ____ (study) for the test at the moment.'
questions.context: Present continuous with the verb to be, Guayanilla, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect! The auxiliary 'is' belongs to the second and third persons, and the subject of this sentence is the pronoun 'I'.
Incorrect! After 'am' the verb must be the participle 'studying', so the base form is impossible.
Correct! The pronoun 'I' always takes the auxiliary 'am', which is followed by the participle 'studying'.
Incorrect! 'Study' is the simple present, and the marker 'at the moment' asks for an action happening now.

questions.explanation:
La conjugacion de 'to be' en presente es I am, you are, he, she e it is, y nosotros, ustedes y ellos son are. Solo el auxiliar cambia de forma; el gerundio del verbo principal se mantiene igual en todas las personas.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'The children ____ (play) in the park every afternoon.'
questions.context: Present continuous with the verb to be, Trujillo Alto, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect! 'Is' is the singular auxiliary, and the subject 'the children' is plural.
Incorrect! 'Plays' is the simple present of a singular subject, and 'every afternoon' describes a habit rather than an action in progress.
Correct! 'The children' is plural, so the auxiliary of the present continuous is 'are' in front of 'playing'.
Incorrect! 'Play' is the bare form, and the progressive with 'the children' would need 'are playing'.

questions.explanation:
Hay que distinguir el uso habitual del uso actual. El presente continuo con 'every afternoon' suena poco natural porque esa expresion marca repeticion; aun asi la frase no es incorrecta si el hablante quiere decir que estan jugando en este momento. El contexto decide cual es la opcion mas natural.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct tag: 'They are coming tonight, ____?'
questions.context: Present continuous question tags, Barceloneta, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Correct! A tag built on a positive present continuous clause takes the negative of the same auxiliary, which gives 'aren't they'.
Incorrect! 'Isn't' is singular, and the subject of the main clause is the plural 'they'.
Incorrect! 'Don't' cannot negate the auxiliary 'are', because a tag repeats the auxiliary of the clause it closes.
Incorrect! 'They are not' is a statement of its own, and a question tag must be a short contracted question.

questions.explanation:
El question tag reutiliza el auxiliar de la frase principal e invierte la polaridad. En presente continuo el tag se construye con el mismo 'to be' del enunciado: 'isn't he', 'aren't they', 'am not I' en las formas contractas mas usadas.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'They ____ (lie) on the beach this afternoon.'
questions.context: Present continuous with spelling changes, Maunabo, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect! 'Lieing' adds an extra e before -ing, and the spelling of 'to lie' stays unchanged in the participle.
Incorrect! 'Lain' is the past participle, which needs 'have' and describes a finished action rather than one in progress.
Incorrect! 'Is lying' uses the singular auxiliary, and the subject of this sentence is the plural 'they'.
Correct! 'They' takes the plural auxiliary 'are', and 'lie' keeps its spelling in front of the participle -ing.

questions.explanation:
Algunos verbos cambian de forma al pasar al gerundio. 'To lie' da 'lying', 'to die' da 'dying' e 'to tie' da 'tying'. En estos casos la vocal breve tensa se convierte en una vocal larga y la -y se mantiene sin duplicar la consonante.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is correct?
questions.context: Present continuous with adverbs of frequency, Yauco, grado 11, W02.

options.text: He never is late for class.
options.feedback: Incorrect! English never splits the present continuous around the adverb, so 'never is late' is not a natural order.

options.text: He is never late for class.
options.feedback: Correct! The adverb 'never' sits between the auxiliary 'is' and the adjective, which is the natural order in English.

options.text: He is late never for class.
options.feedback: Incorrect! 'Late never' pushes the adverb to the end of the clause, and no English clause allows that position here.
Incorrect! 'Never' without any auxiliary leaves the verb with no tense at all, and English always needs one.

questions.explanation:
La negacion del presente continuo se puede hacer de dos maneras equivalentes: con el auxiliar 'not' o con adverbios como 'never', 'always' o 'often'. En ambos casos el orden es auxiliar, adverbio y gerundio, con el adverbio pegado al auxiliar.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'She ____ (teach) biology at the high school.'
questions.context: Present continuous with the verb to be, Cayey, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect! 'Teach ing' splits one word into two, and a participle is always written as a single word.
Correct! 'Is teaching' is the auxiliary 'is' plus the participle 'teaching', which is exactly the present continuous.
Incorrect! 'Teaches' is the simple present, and the question asks for the progressive form.
Incorrect! 'Teatching' mis-spells the base verb, and a participle can never change the spelling of the stem.

questions.explanation:
Cuando el verbo termina en vocal mas -e la -e desaparece antes de -ing, como en 'teach' que da 'teaching' o 'dance' que da 'dancing'. La duplicacion de consonante se reserva para vocal breve tensa, por lo que 'teaching' lleva una sola -t.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'He ____ (write) an email to his teacher right now.'
questions.context: Present continuous with the verb to write, San Sebastian, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect! 'Writeing' keeps the silent e before -ing, and a verb ending in -e simply drops it.
Incorrect! 'Writting' doubles a consonant that this verb never doubles, so the participle keeps a single t.
Incorrect! 'Writes' is the simple present of a singular subject, while the marker 'right now' asks for the progressive.
Correct! 'Is writing' is the auxiliary 'is' followed by the participle 'writing', with no extra letter anywhere.

questions.explanation:
Los verbos terminados en -w con vocal breve tensa forman el gerundio duplicando la consonante: 'write' da 'writing'. En cambio los terminados en -e como 'dance' o 'smile' solo pierden la -e y no duplican nada. Reconocer la vocal evita confundir ambos grupos.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct form: '____ you waiting for the results?'
questions.context: Present continuous in the negative question, Camuy, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect! 'Do' builds questions with action verbs in the simple present, but 'waiting' is a participle.
Incorrect! 'Is' is the singular auxiliary, and the subject 'you' always takes the plural one.
Correct! 'You' takes the plural auxiliary 'Are', which is followed by the participle 'waiting' in this question.
Incorrect! 'Am' belongs to the pronoun 'I', and the subject of this question is 'you'.

questions.explanation:
En una pregunta el auxiliar 'to be' abre la frase y decide la concordancia con el sujeto. El gerundio no lleva auxiliar propio y simplemente sigue al verbo 'to be'. Cualquier otra forma de auxiliar rompe la estructura del presente continuo.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: What does this sentence express? 'We are meeting the teacher tomorrow at ten.'
questions.context: Present continuous with future meaning, Luquillo, grado 11, W02.

options.text: An arrangement for a future time.
options.feedback: Correct! An arrangement such as 'We are meeting the teacher tomorrow at ten' uses 'be' plus the participle, which signals a fixed plan rather than a guess.

options.text: An action that is happening right now.
options.feedback: Incorrect! 'An action that is happening right now' would need 'tomorrow at ten' to point at this moment, and it does not.
Incorrect! 'A habit from the past' describes a repeated action that stopped, which the present continuous can never express.
Incorrect! 'A prediction about the future' is made with 'will' plus a base verb, and this sentence contains no modal.

questions.explanation:
El presente continuo tiene un uso especial con el futuro: un acuerdo o plan definido. Cuando hay una hora exacta y un compromiso asumido, como 'we are meeting tomorrow at ten', la frase describe algo futuro pero seguro y ya organizado.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Question: 'Are you eating lunch now?' Answer: '____'
questions.context: Present continuous in short answers, Toa Baja, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Correct! 'Yes, I am' repeats the auxiliary of the question and adds nothing else, which is the standard short answer.
Incorrect! 'Yes, I eat' repeats the simple present instead of the auxiliary, so it does not answer a continuous question.
Incorrect! 'Yes, I am eating' adds a new piece of information, and a short answer only agrees with the question.
Incorrect! 'Yes, I do' uses the auxiliary of an action verb, but the question was built with 'are'.

questions.explanation:
Las respuestas cortas siguen el mismo auxiliar que la pregunta. Si la pregunta abre con 'are', la respuesta abre con 'am' para 'I'; si abre con 'do', la respuesta abre con 'do'. Ignorar el auxiliar cambia el tiempo verbal de la respuesta.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence is not natural in English?
questions.context: Present continuous with state verbs, Naguabo, grado 11, W02.

options.text: An action that is happening right now.
options.feedback: Incorrect! 'An action that is happening right now' is a perfectly natural use of the present continuous, so this reading does not make the sentence unnatural.
Incorrect! 'A habit from the past' could never be what this sentence means, so this reading is not the reason to reject it.
Incorrect! 'A prediction about the future' is not what this sentence says either, because it contains no modal at all.

options.text: An arrangement for a future time.
options.feedback: Correct! 'An arrangement for a future time' is the odd reading here, because the present continuous marks actions in progress or habits rather than a fixed future plan.

questions.explanation:
Ciertos verbos de estado, como 'to know', 'to love', 'to want' o 'to believe', no se usan normalmente en presente continuo. Se expresan con presente simple, porque describen una situacion permanente y no una actividad en curso.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Complete the sentence: 'Look! The bus ____ (come) around the corner.'
questions.context: Present continuous with the verb to go, Hatillo, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect! 'Comes' is the simple present, and the marker 'Look!' signals an action in progress at this moment.
Correct! The marker 'Look!' always introduces the present continuous, which here is 'is' plus 'coming'.
Incorrect! After 'is' the verb must be the participle 'coming', and the base form is impossible there.
Incorrect! 'Comming' doubles the m, and English never writes two of the same consonant in a stem like this.

questions.explanation:
Verbos como 'look', 'listen' y 'now' indican que algo esta pasando en el momento en que se habla. En esos casos el presente continuo es obligatorio, y el gerundio se forma quitando la -e final del verbo cuando existe.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Choose the correct tag: 'I am not tired yet, ____?'
questions.context: Present continuous question tags, Yabucoa, grado 11, W02.

options.feedback: Incorrect! 'Aren't I' is not a possible contraction, because 'am' never shortens to 'aren't' anywhere in English.
Incorrect! 'Do I not' negates an action verb, and the verb of this clause is the one of 'to be'.
Correct! A tag on a negative clause keeps the same auxiliary in its full form, which gives 'am I not'.
Incorrect! 'Isn't I' mixes two different auxiliaries, and 'am' is the only one that agrees with the pronoun 'I'.

questions.explanation:
En presente continuo el tag se construye con el mismo auxiliar de la frase principal. Con 'I' ese auxiliar es 'am', de modo que la forma contracta mas usual es "aren't I" en la afirmacion y "am I" en la negacion, que es la unica combinacion posible.
